goals: Restore Minecraft 26.2's normal biome-specific vanilla village composition while preserving Matcha's village eligibility and sparse placement layer.
Keep Matcha as the sole owner of the minecraft:villages structure-set placement contract.
Provide the restoration as a Fabric mod whose required built-in server-data pack deterministically outranks Matcha without modifying or redistributing Matcha.
scope: Package exactly one built-in server-data pack containing pack.mcmeta and five complete minecraft:village_* structure overrides for plains, desert, savanna, snowy, and taiga villages.
Preserve Matcha's exact biome arrays while restoring each pristine vanilla 26.2 style-specific start pool and all other vanilla jigsaw fields.
Register that exact nested pack as ALWAYS_ENABLED and move only its exact pack ID to Minecraft's final, highest-priority resource position while preserving every other pack's relative order.

Retain Matcha's spacing 80, separation 50, salt 10387312 candidate lattice without claiming identical realized starts at eligible-biome boundaries, where the changed start-template anchor can affect the jigsaw biome check.

exclusions: Any minecraft:villages structure-set override, additional structure ID, biome tag, template pool, processor, NBT template, loot table, trade, function, or Java recreation of the five village definitions.
Global reordering of arbitrary packs or resource-level enforcement beyond promoting the single exact Matcha Vanilla Village Restoration built-in pack ID.
Modification of Matcha itself, resource-pack work, Stack to Nearby Chests work, or Quick Stack Nearby work.
Conversion claims for existing generated villages or guarantees of seed-identical realized starts at eligible-biome boundaries.
Runtime deployment, Test Slot or Test Instance Manager changes, dedicated Workbench profile access, and protected gameplay-instance access during this migration.
